body:
OBSERVED 2026-08-21 on the operator's own Kobo Clara BW (firmware 4.45.23792),
read-only copy of KoboReader.sqlite, mode=ro + PRAGMA query_only.

This is the #1657 fragment defect caught in the wild, on real user data, and it is
the concrete evidence that makes F-3e383a matter.

## The measurement

Applying #1657's own render predicate -- Nickel renders a Bookmark only when
Bookmark.ContentID exactly equals a content row with ContentType=9 -- to all 30
annotations on the device:

    Bookmark rows total              30   (17 highlight + 13 dogear)
    RENDERABLE (ContentType=9 match) 28
    NOT renderable                    2

The two that fail:

    The Able McLaughlins  dogear  created 2026-08-18T01:47:36
      ...!OEBPS!902696697345144105_59845-h-0.htm.xhtml#pgepubid00001
    The Age of Innocence  dogear  created 2026-08-18T01:51:09
      ...!OEBPS!7492349454248664808_541-h-0.htm.xhtml#pgepubid00008

Both carry a #fragment. A chapter identity with a fragment matches no ContentType=9
spine row, so Nickel cannot render the annotation anchored to it. That is exactly
the defect #1657 describes and #1773 fixes.

## Why this is F-3e383a's evidence, not a new bug

The forward fix has shipped. These two annotations are still broken because the
books were ALREADY DELIVERED to the device before it. F-3e383a is precisely the
finding that a KEPUB repair may never reach a device that already holds the book:
kepub_package_repair calls mark_book_modified(..., unsync=False), so
remove_synced_book -- the step whose own docstring describes it as what makes
every device re-pull -- never runs.

So the state on real hardware is: the defect is fixed for new deliveries, and two
of the operator's real annotations remain unrenderable on their device with no
mechanism to heal them. That is the gap F-3e383a names, now with a measured
consequence attached rather than a hypothetical one.

## Scope and honesty

- Both affected rows are DOGEARS, not highlights. All 17 highlights render.
  Impact is real but smaller than the raw 2/30 suggests -- a lost dogear is a lost
  place-marker, not lost user-authored text.
- I did NOT attempt a repair-and-redeliver to confirm the healing path, because
  that requires the armed F-3e383a experiment and a device sync, and a failed
  checkforchanges download makes Nickel replace the local annotation set with
  EMPTY. KoboReader.sqlite is read-only by standing rule, so a wipe would be
  unrecoverable. ASSUMED, not observed: that re-delivery would fix these two.
- Device-side capture kept out of the repo and deleted once it stops being evidence.
title: Two of the operator's real annotations are unrenderable on hardware: the #1657 fragment defect, measured in the wild
